import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 28

References:
- [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.28)
- [Mathoverflow/339137](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/339137/why-do-polynomials-with-coefficients-0-1-like-to-have-only-factors-with-0-1) asked by user [Sil](https://mathoverflow.net/users/136794/sil)
- [MathStackexchange/3325163](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3325163/) asked by user [Emmanuel Amiot](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/403309/emmanuel-amiot)
-/

namespace Green28

/-- True if a PMF on $\mathbb{Z}$ is uniformly distributed on its support. -/
def IsUniformOnSupport (X : PMF ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : Finset ℤ) (hs : s.Nonempty), X = PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs

/--
The discrete convolution of two PMFs on $\mathbb{Z}$, representing the distribution of the sum of
two independent random variables.
-/
noncomputable def indepSum (X Y : PMF ℤ) : PMF ℤ := do
  let x ← X
  let y ← Y
  PMF.pure (x + y)

/--
Suppose that $X, Y$ are two finitely-supported independent random variables taking integer values,
and such that $X + Y$ is uniformly distributed on its range. Are $X$ and $Y$ themselves uniformly
distributed on their ranges?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 60]
theorem green_28 : answer(sorry) ↔
  ∀ (X Y : PMF ℤ), -- marginals, independence is built into indepSum
    X.support.Finite ∧ Y.support.Finite ∧ IsUniformOnSupport (indepSum X Y) →
      IsUniformOnSupport X ∧ IsUniformOnSupport Y := by
  sorry

end Green28

reformulations.difference: The existential finset is not explicitly required to equal the PMF’s support.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib’s uniformOfFinset assigns mass |s|⁻¹ on the nonempty finset s and zero elsewhere, and support_uniformOfFinset proves its support is exactly ↑s. In the scratch file, I proved the definition equivalent to ∃ s, s.Nonempty ∧ X.support = ↑s ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, X x = (s.card : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹. Thus the omitted explicit support equality does not weaken the definition.

reformulations.difference: The theorem quantifies over marginal PMFs and constructs indepSum, rather than quantifying over independent random variables on a probability space.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Independent integer-valued random variables with marginal laws p and q have sum law ∑ₓ p(x)q(z−x), exactly the product-weighted convolution defined by indepSum. Conversely, every pair of PMFs is realized by the independent coordinate variables under the product probability measure on ℤ × ℤ. Finite support and uniformity depend only on these laws, so both formulations quantify over precisely the same possibilities. The convolution formula was checked in Lean, but the full random-variable equivalence was not formalized.
